description: The bar chart illustrates the bias percentage across three different contact conditions—Support of Authorities, Extended Contact, and Virtual Contact—before and after exposure to various types of contact, as measured by the model's responses. The vertical axis represents the bias percentage, ranging from 0 to 70, while the horizontal axis categorizes the three contact conditions. For each condition, there are four bars representing different contact types: "No Contact Before" (light gray), "Positive Contact Before" (light red), "Negative Contact Before" (light blue), and "No Contact After" (dark gray with diagonal stripes), "Positive Contact After" (dark red with diagonal stripes), and "Negative Contact After" (dark blue with diagonal stripes). In the "Support of Authorities" category, the bias percentages are 39.50 for No Contact Before, 31.83 for Positive Contact Before, and 42.38 for Negative Contact Before, with all "After" contact types showing a bias of 0.00. In the "Extended Contact" category, the bias percentages are 40.61 for No Contact Before, 36.13 for Positive Contact Before, and 47.28 for Negative Contact Before, with all "After" contact types again showing a bias of 0.00. In the "Virtual Contact" category, the bias percentages are 39.74 for No Contact Before, 39.17 for Positive Contact Before, and 43.83 for Negative Contact Before, with the "No Contact After" group showing a bias of 10.00, the "Positive Contact After" group showing a bias of 10.01, and the "Negative Contact After" group showing a bias of 10.02. The chart indicates that the bias percentage is generally lower in the "After" contact groups compared to the "Before" contact groups, with the "After" contact groups showing a bias of 0.00 in the "Support of Authorities" and "Extended Contact" categories, and a bias of 10.00 or higher in the "Virtual Contact" category. The "No Contact After" group shows a bias of 10.00 in the "Virtual Contact" category, while the "Positive Contact After" and "Negative Contact After" groups show a bias of 10.01 and 10.02, respectively. The chart also shows that the bias percentage is generally higher in the "Negative Contact Before" group compared to the "Positive Contact Before" group in all three categories.
